[b]A game of chess on a Tartakani board[/b]

As RJR troops landed at airfields in Tartakum, they weren't the only ones offloading weapons. Rutan Armed Security guards offloaded their own discrete equipment and vehicles, planning for not a battle of force, but of marketing and representation. Them, along with the RJR, were meant to provide security to the mining operations and secure lavian influence in the region. The government couldnt have Sumitone and their commie friends running needed trade routes and corrupt a potential ally. The RJR would be for a bit of a good show and convincing the locals that they needed lavian expertise, and the RAS would combat any espionage SummitOne would take against Lavian interests, and convince companies that they need armed security. 

As soon as the RJR moved out to support the rag tag Tartakani army, the RAS guards moved their loaded trucks out to the mining sites. There, they would set up barbed wire fencing, checkpoints, cameras, everything you would need to keep people out and observe those who are in. While the RJR was busy training some men in how to fight insurgents, they visited local shops and gathering places, building rapport and networks of friends. Of course, they werent the only ones on special missions. The Makinar Military Intelligence Bureau was busying themselves with looking over every inch and system of the ZTZ-65 tanks loaned to the RJR, a vital insight into [nation]Qianxun[/nation] armored technology. 

So there they sat, standing guard, protecting the mines, sometimes telling off kids who wanted to take a look at all the big dump trucks. Slowly, they became familiar to the locals, a relation which would be necessary to claw influence from the hands of those deemed to not have Lavias best interests in mind.
